scope: AC03 participation by two existing, independently distributed MCP clients; no provider or new native adapter

clients.name: @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
clients.invocation: node <temporary inspector-client.mjs>; private fixture input arrives on stdin
clients.qualification: Distributed programmatic Inspector modules, not the standalone Inspector CLI
clients.cli_limit: Its launcher converts config headers to --header child argv. The qualification bypasses that launcher and passes in-memory headers to the existing transport factory. It implements no JSON-RPC or HTTP client itself.

clients.name: fastmcp
clients.runtime: Python 3.13.1 with -I and explicit code/dependency paths
clients.invocation: python -I <temporary fastmcp-client.py>; private fixture input arrives on stdin
clients.qualification: FastMCP Client programmatic API, separate process and implementation from Inspector

minimal_flow: Start the existing RestartServer owner helper against current selected Nexus imports and a disposable home. Local discovery is explicitly empty; no native adapter is composed.

Seed exactly two synthetic agent identities, private fixture keys and one logical workspace through existing repositories/auth service. Snapshot identities and execution bindings after real Server readiness.
Each separate client performs tools/list and session_open with its own authenticated identity. Keep session_secret only in that client process; assert two canonical active sessions.

Inspector calls message_create directed to FastMCP. FastMCP calls inbox_pull and inbox_ack, then message_create with parent_message_id replying to Inspector. Inspector receives and acknowledges the exact reply.

Disconnect/reconnect MCP transport in each client; heartbeat the same canonical session, do not reopen sessions or identities. Assert unchanged identity/binding set, canonical message correlation, and zero runtime sessions/operations.
Close clients with exit0 required, invoke the Server canonical stop and verify owner exit/listener closure. Cleanup joins all owned processes even on an assertion failure.
